lines.text: Every Friday afternoon, the canteen of our school turns into a sorting station.
The recycling drive was started two years ago by five student who were
tired of seeing full rubbish bins. They place three large boxes near the
lines.note: Tense: 'placed … and asked' — both verbs are in the past.

lines.text: drink stall and asked his schoolmates to bring paper, cans and plastic bottles.
lines.note: Pronoun: 'they' is plural, so it is 'their schoolmates'.

lines.text: At first, the response was disappointed, and some people even threw food into
lines.note: Word form: the response is 'disappointing'; a person feels 'disappointed'.

lines.text: the boxes. The team did not give up. They spoke at assembly, made
posters and showed a video who explained where the school’s rubbish goes.
lines.note: 'Who' is for people. A video takes 'that' or 'which'.

lines.text: Slowly, the boxes began to fill. Today, each class have its own monitor,
lines.note: Agreement: 'each class' is singular, so it is 'has'.

lines.text: and the items are weighed before a collection lorry arrives. The class that
collects the more receives a small prize at the end of each term.
lines.note: Superlative: among all the classes it is 'the most'.

lines.text: The founders have since graduated, but younger students have taken over of them.
What began as a small complaint has become a habit for everyone.
